 Trump Says "I Don't Know" on Summit with Kim Jong-un... Adjusting Pace
 Lee Hanseok 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.10.20 06:26 
 View 
 View Count 
 PIP 닫기 
 [Anchor] 
 U.S. President Donald Trump has responded that he does not know when asked whether he could meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un on the sidelines of the APEC summit to be held in China next month. This marks a sudden shift from his repeated claims that they would meet within the year, which is seen as an effort to adjust his pace as North Korea shows little sign of responding. 
 Here is a report from Washington correspondent Lee Hanseok. 
 [Reporter] 
 Meeting with reporters at the White House, U.S. President Donald Trump. 
 When asked if he could meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un on the occasion of attending the APEC summit to be held in Shenzhen, China, next month, he gave an unexpected answer. 
 [Donald Trump / U.S. President: I get along very well with Kim Jong-un. I get along with him very well, and I don't know who is asking for a meeting, but my relationship with Kim Jong-un is very good.] 
 While repeatedly emphasizing his personal ties with Chairman Kim, he retreated to a reserved stance regarding whether an actual meeting would take place, saying it was unclear if it was wanted. 
 Just a week ago, President Trump did not hide his expectations regarding the possibility of a meeting with Chairman Kim, stating that it could happen and that it would be thrilling if it did. 
 He even specifically mentioned North Korea's nuclear stockpile and made remarks that virtually seemed to recognize it as a nuclear weapons state, urging unconditional dialogue. 
 However, despite President Trump's courtship, which had guaranteed a North Korea-U.S. summit within the year, North Korea has maintained a silent response. 
 Analysts suggest that as North Korea shows an attitude of trying to shake things up by focusing on its military closeness with Russia rather than responding to America's overtures for dialogue, President Trump has also hidden his impatience and begun adjusting his tone. 
 As President Trump has initiated a pace adjustment for now, the possibility of a dramatic North Korea-U.S. showdown on the APEC stage has become increasingly uncertain.
